sylvie (eng-runtime): heads up — seen steady memory growth on rk-infer-07 over ~12h when serving long-context chat sessions. spikes at ~8k tokens then slow drift afterwards. attaching short profiler dump below.

omar (eng-runtime): yeah noticed that on canary too. looks like free pool fragmentation? can you paste the sample?

sylvie (eng-runtime): pasted below. it's an ascii heatmap from kv-sampler. key thing: lot of tiny 64B/128B blocks scattered, plus some large 32k blocks that never get reused.

```
KV-sample heatmap (most recent):
hot slots: 16k-32k (20% reuse)
small slots: 64-512 (3% reuse)
fragmentation estimate: 11.3% (up from 2.1% at startup)
longctx-preserve: 14.7% of total pages pinned
```

lin (eng-performance): that pattern screams mixed-allocation churn. long contexts allocate large tail blocks for KV pages, but intermediate edits sprinkle small allocations. allocator coalescing isn't catching because buddy boundaries misalign.

tess (eng-sre): what's the evict/async-pager behavior right now? are we paging to disk or to per-model spill?

sylvie (eng-runtime): currently async-pager moves cold slabs to host RAM or spills to tmpfs when under memory pressure. we don't compact across slab classes. evict rate modest — but compaction never triggers because fragmentation threshold uses global free ratio, which stays ok. problem is internal fragmentation within slab classes.

omar (eng-runtime): oh — so thresholding by global free ratio hides intra-slab holes. I propose we add per-slab fragmentation tracking and a hysteresis compaction trigger: if slab-frag > 8% for > 30m, schedule background relink/compact.

lin (eng-performance): +1. couple follow-ups: (1) prefer incremental relocation of live entries rather than whole-slab pauses; (2) prioritize slabs with mixed-size churn based on a churn-score; (3) try reserving a small tail pool for long-context allocations to avoid interleaving.

sylvie (eng-runtime): sketch for incremental compactor: drain N blocks at a time, move live KV to fresh slab, update pointers via indirection table, free old blocks. we can do this lock-free per-core using per-core move-queues. should avoid lat spikes if N small.

alloc-bot: compaction-scan-report node=rk-infer-07 start=1746600300 reclaimed=0MB reason="below-global-threshold" fragments=11.28%

omar (eng-runtime): alloc-bot confirms current policy. we need a small simulation before rollout. can someone run the frag-sim with a longctx trace? sylvie can you export 10k token workload trace?

sylvie (eng-runtime): uploaded to /tmp/longctx-trace-10k.json on canary, and pushed a test harness to the perf repo (pr #472). instructions in the README: run `./tools/frag-sim --trace /tmp/longctx-trace-10k.json --epochs 3`

lin (eng-performance): ran 3 epochs locally. baseline (no incremental compact): fragmentation goes 2% -> 12% -> 14% and resident grows ~620MB. prototype incremental compact (N=64 moves/sec) yields frag plateau at ~3.8% and resident stabilizes +90MB. p99 CPU up ~3%.

tess (eng-sre): 3% p99 CPU impact is tolerable if latency unaffected. can we gate this behind a per-customer opt-in for Dedicated?

omar (eng-runtime): yes gate + rollout: feature flag `kv_inc_compact` default off for Hosted, opt-in for Dedicated. implement metrics: slab_frag_pct, compacts/sec, move_backlog. add trace context to requests touching relocated keys.

sylvie (eng-runtime): additional mitigation: tune small-block bin sizes — making 64B->96B quantization reduced tiny-block churn in sim by 27%. we should test a hybrid binning: 64/96/128/256 instead of current powers-of-two.

lin (eng-performance): curious tradeoff: larger base bins reduce internal fragmentation for many small allocations but raise peak RL usage. in sim the resident delta was +12MB but frag dropped significantly. might be a win.

tess (eng-sre): operational checklist for rollout? we should have: 1) safety kill-switch, 2) onboarded metrics/dashboards, 3) canary on 1-2 hosts, 4) evacuation plan if p99 latency regresses.

omar (eng-runtime): agreed. I'll open an RFC summarizing triggers, compactor design (incremental movers, per-slab thresholds), binning experiment, and the perf numbers. target review EOD tomorrow.

sylvie (eng-runtime): thanks — tagging folks for follow-up: @lin for perf sign-off, @tess for ops runbook, and @alloc-bot to watch the scheduled scans. I'll loop back with microbenchmark results for hybrid binning. :thumbsup:
